comments.body:
# Session: cut Gerrit Verified gate wall-clock without losing coverage

## Question
"How can we reduce the wall-clock runtime of our Gerrit Verified Gate on GitHub Actions
without reducing our coverage?" Operator later reported real gate times of 41-47 min.

## What the measurements showed
- Critical path was ONE job: `pytest (macos-latest, py3.13)` at 18.6m (run #1823 /
  id 30569775555). Every other job <=8m; without macOS the run finishes in ~8m.
- Within it: setup 0.7m, twelve drift gates ~0.1m, default pytest tier 15.4m, integration 2.0m.
- 7856 tests: ubuntu 5:04 at -n 4 vs macOS 15:21 at -n 3 — a 3x wall gap against a 1.33x vCPU gap.
- Dispatch lag from Gerrit is NOT a factor: change 1052 ps1 uploaded 18:24:36, run created
  18:24:38 (2s), Verified+1 at 18:53:35 = 29.0m, matching GitHub's own run_duration_ms.
- THE BINDING CONSTRAINT: navapbc is on GitHub Free = 20 concurrent jobs / 5 macOS,
  enforced PER ORGANIZATION, shared with every other navapbc repo. A single Verified run
  needs 21 job slots — one run alone cannot fully parallelize. Six changes dispatched within
  10 seconds queued 6.7-8.4m each for a macOS slot. That queue is the 41-47m.
- Peak concurrent macOS jobs observed across 25 sampled jobs: 4, never more.

## What landed (5 changes, all merged, all tickets closed)
| Change | Ticket | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| 1056 | f3d4 | coverage collected on ubuntu cells only (measured +5.1% overhead, so ~0.8m) |
| 1063 | 699f | store template + copy-per-test: tests/interfaces 270.7s -> 186.5s at -n 4 (31%) |
| 1065 | 2132 | deleted redundant import-linter job, repaid with a durable collection guard |
| 1066 | ad63 | optionality fan-out 6 jobs -> 1 venv loop (7 iterations, 7 venvs) |
| 1070 | 446c | template-virginity assertion moved into the fixture |

Coverage went UP, not down: `metrics` is in `_optional.EXTRAS` but had NO per-extra CI
before 1066; the loop now covers it.

## Rejected, with reasons (do not re-propose without new evidence)
- **3-way macOS shard.** `fail_under = 70` is enforced PER pytest session, so every shard
  fails (reproduced: 26.91% on a 4% subset). `.test_durations` is gitignored deliberately by
  ticket 9ad9. The `pytest-split` dep in pyproject was a WAIVED scope-creep finding against
  ticket 8d36, not prior intent. Honest speedup 2.2x not 3x, and it RAISES macOS job-minutes
  18.6 -> 21.0, making the 6-run burst worse (22.3 -> 25.2m). Wins only when R x S <= C, i.e.
  one solitary change.
- **macOS `-n 3 -> 4`.** The IO-bound premise was wrong: serial CPU:wall is 0.71, `-n 3`
  already demands 2.19 of 3 vCPUs, scaling saturates at `-n 6` and REGRESSES at `-n 9` on an
  18-core box, with sys > user throughout (kernel/filesystem contention). Its stated
  precondition (widen tests/scripts/reducer/test_reducer_cache.py:288) targets a test that is
  `skipif(CI == "true")` and never runs in CI. Worth re-deriving now that 1063 removed ~58
  process spawns per interfaces test, since that changes the sys/user balance it rested on.

## Load-bearing facts discovered (cite these, don't re-derive)
- **The Verified gate CANNOT exercise a change to `.github/workflows/**`.** `uses:
  ./.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` resolves from the DEFAULT BRANCH under
  workflow_dispatch; the patchset is only checked out INSIDE jobs. A flat pre-merge number is
  not evidence a workflow change did nothing — verified by dumping the macOS command line on
  1056's own run and finding `--cov` still present.
- **The working pre-merge lane for workflow changes is a SCRATCH BRANCH push to the mirror**
  (`optionality.yml` triggers on push, branches-ignore feature/**). A PULL REQUEST does not
  work: `.github/workflows/lockdown.yml` runs repo-lockdown on pull_request_target with
  close-pr: true. Used successfully on 1066 (run 30591336796).
- **Bare `git worktree repair` is DESTRUCTIVE, not a silent no-op.** Run inside a copy it
  rewrites the SOURCE's `.tickets-tracker/.git` to point into the copy.
- **`--git-common-dir` is green on a half-fixed store copy.** It derives from
  `.tickets-tracker/.git` alone and cannot witness a stale `gitdir`. Use
  `git worktree list --porcelain` containment.
- **`conftest` is not a stable module name.** Several conftests share it; under xdist
  `sys.modules["conftest"]` binds to whichever was imported last. `from conftest import X`
  works when a tier runs alone and fails in a full-suite run. Hence
  `tests/interfaces/_store_template.py`.
- **`init._gen_local_files()` is idempotency-guarded** (`if not os.path.isfile`), so calling
  it to re-mint `.env-id`/`.signing-key` on a copy is a silent no-op.
- **The gate snapshot store is keyed by COMMIT SHA ALONE** (`_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py`), so
  a shared template SHA collapses ~150 gate-touching tests onto one entry. `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR`
  is set per test.
- **`_optional.EXTRAS` != the old per-extra matrix list.** EXTRAS = {agents, eval, grounding,
  metrics, tracing}; `mcp` is NOT in it (no probe; validated by its boot check).
- **The literal `|| { rc=1; ...; continue; }` accumulator trips shellcheck SC2015** through
  actionlint and fails `make lint`. Use `if ! { ...; }; then ...; fi`.

## Process notes
Five review rounds each found something real; two layers caught different classes — rebar's
plan gate found unproven ACs and a false factual claim, subagents found mechanism bugs.
My own recurring error: asserting a safety property in the ACs while the mechanism I specified
could not deliver it (a `--git-common-dir` guard that passes on the broken case; a
`list_tickets`-based isolation check that reads worktree files, not refs; a claimed PR
validation lane that auto-closes). Validating 1063 by running `tests/interfaces` alone was the
one scope where its bug was invisible — the full suite caught it.

## Left open
- `docs/llm-framework.md` "The optional surface is three extras" is stale: `_optional.EXTRAS`
  has five. Needs new descriptive content for `grounding` and `metrics` — separate ticket.
- Deferred from 699f: ~20 module-local fixtures in tests/interfaces still build stores the old
  way. Migrating them onto `_clone_template` is the larger remaining share of that win.

Bug-trend analysis (2026-08-01), full reviewed detail. Basis for the change-review walkthrough and the forthcoming approved-changes epic. Originally drafted into idea ticket e71b-1a38-bf7a-4de0; canonical copy now here.

# rebar bug-trend analysis (2026-08-01, reviewed)

Data baseline: 344 bug tickets (77 Jun, 260 Jul, 7 Aug 1); 333 closed. Bug-close `--class`
enum (regression | plan_defect | env_integration | flaky | preexisting | not_a_bug |
duplicate | escalated | undetermined) became required ~07-19 (ed13); 214 closed bugs carry
no class — ~207 predate the requirement, ~7 post-date it via then-unenforced close surfaces
(the 376d class: MCP transition / NDJSON import). Of the 119 classified: preexisting 57,
plan_defect 15, env_integration 14, duplicate 12, regression 12, not_a_bug 4, flaky 4,
undetermined 1. Caveat: every classified close is a July/Aug-created bug (the June cohort
closed pre-taxonomy), and the class is closer-self-reported, unaudited. Tags: 237/344
untagged, ad-hoc vocab.
creation_channel: unknown 209 / cli 126 / jira 5 / python 4. file_impact set on 100/344.
`rebar metrics` registry lenses: agent_process (attempts_per_ticket, first_pass_rate,
reopen_recovery, revert_recovery, rework_within_7_days), code_health (churn,
refactor_to_addition_ratio), gate_economics (cost_per_accepted_change,
first_pass_verification, env_diagnosis_intervals); module-size metrics show `unavailable`.
No bug lens exists.

Title-keyword clustering (overlapping, 261/344 matched):
reconciler/Jira sync 77; concurrency/locking/git-store races 76; plan-review/attestation
gate defects 55; CI/test flakiness+isolation 41; silent-failure/fail-open 39; infra/deploy
27; code-review gate 24; completion-verifier/close gate 22; config/env-var 19;
truncation/pagination/limits 15; direction-inversion/asymmetry ~7.

Recurring same-class families (explicit in titles): unlocked raw git commits bypassing the
canonical locked write seam (3a33, 3435, 4dd2, 3b4e); pagination truncation (9263, 1f3d,
deac); link-direction inversion (3b86 → 4b59 → 32cc); asymmetric ADD-only differs (7f42,
908c); lock wedges/reclamation (620c, a4b2, 304e, ac26, 1a47, 9305, 449f — 449f documents 7
post-fix recurrences as residual, not regression); mtime-less cache staleness (1d76, e995,
908b); wall-clock perf assertions in tests (edfe, b228, 19d7, 5e94, 85c3); missing
subprocess timeouts (c16f, d843, 747f); "exists on CLI only, not lib/MCP" parity (6e88,
1598, 5199, d21b; close --class rollout misses 0e15, 376d); unread config/env keys (281f,
9d7a; b00f is the adjacent scanner-blind-spot case).

---

## Q1 — Additional observability/traceability? YES, three low/zero-friction gaps.

What already exists and costs users nothing extra: bug-close `--class` (bounded enum,
enforced); the **blame-hunt subsystem** — every bug close best-effort auto-derives a
`caused_by` link to the culprit ticket (`src/rebar/metrics/blame.py`,
`transition_close.py:490`, ticket 555e) with retroactive backfills
(`scripts/backfill_caused_by.py`, `scripts/backfill_bug_class.py` — structural, no-LLM
close_class backfill from reverts/REVIEW_RESULT/gate_error signals, ticket 5062);
`discovered_from` links; tags; session logs; auto-filed canary tickets (binding-drift,
heartbeat) with a find-existing-then-comment dedup pattern; the code-review FP ledger
(`fp:code-review` bug tickets with a `root-cause:` enum, compiled into NO-FIRE eval cases);
`rebar metrics` lenses.

Gaps:
1. **The close taxonomy captures relationship-to-work, not mechanism or escape channel.**
   `preexisting` (57/119) tells you it wasn't a regression; it does not tell you it was a
   concurrency bug that escaped because no gate looks at raw git writes. Recommendation:
   a **batch auto-classifier** extending the 5062 backfill pattern — structural signals
   where they suffice, the `rebar.llm` framework for the rest — writing bounded
   `mechanism:*` / `detected-by:*` tags to closed bugs on a schedule, spot-checked. Zero
   author burden. Do NOT add a second *required* close flag: the `--class` rollout itself
   broke every automated close surface (0e15 red main; 376d MCP/NDJSON gaps; the canary
   closes bugs programmatically — reconcile-bridge-canary.yml:300), and automation would
   stamp a constant value anyway, polluting the data.
2. **Nothing aggregates.** Answering "top bug mechanism this month" required re-mining 344
   titles by hand; the registry has agent_process/code_health/gate_economics lenses but no
   bug lens. Recommendation: a `bug_trends` metrics lens over data already in the store —
   close_class distribution over time, mechanism-tag distribution, open-bug age,
   `caused_by` fan-in (shared culprits), canary time-to-detect. Read-only; zero burden.
3. **Class-level recurrence is prose; only culprit-level links are structured.**
   `caused_by` gives queryable bug→culprit-ticket links, but "same class as the
   enrich-queue prune race", "sibling sweep of 5546", "9305 rec #1" live in titles —
   recurrence-of-a-mechanism across channels is unqueryable. Recommendation: a link/tag
   convention (`relates_to` to the anchor bug + a `class:<anchor>` tag) written by the
   debug skill automatically (see Q4), so recurrence rate per class becomes a query.
Also: extend the FP-ledger pattern (proven for code review) to plan-review false positives —
a large fraction of the 55 plan-review bugs are FP/noise reports; making each a NO-FIRE eval
case compounds precision.
Anti-recommendation: no new mandatory fields at bug **create** time (canaries and agents
must file cheaply), and no mandatory prose root-cause field (comments already carry it).

## Q2 — Fragility/decay trends? Mostly surface-expansion + latent-defect discovery, with four real structural weaknesses.

The July spike tracks new subsystem activation (review-bot, auto-lander, Bedrock cutover,
Jira DC, live tiers); the June baseline was itself audit-driven (audit-2026-06-09 filed ~17
on 06-10; antipattern-audit). In the classified (July-created, self-reported) subsample,
`preexisting` outnumbers `regression` 57:12 — consistent with latent-defect discovery
rather than decay, though that subsample excludes the June cohort and is unaudited. Four
structural fragility patterns are real and mitigable regardless:
1. **A bespoke concurrent database on git** (~76 bugs). Many writers (CLI, MCP, review-bot,
   reconcile-bridge, enrich queue, janitors, retention) re-discover the locking contract;
   failures: unlocked whole-index commits, auto-gc/maintenance corrupting the shared object
   DB, unreclaimable locks in containers. Mitigation: one canonical locked write seam
   (`run_git_write` exists; delete/txn/compact/init already route through it), **enforced
   deterministically in CI** — forbid raw `git commit`/index mutation outside an
   allowlisted seam, scoped to store-touching code AND workflows/scripts:
   reconcile-bridge.yml:283 does a raw `git commit` of ticket events in CI and is the live
   instance behind 449f's dominant failure mode; a src/rebar-only lint would miss it.
   Allowlist the seam files and test-fixture repos (eval_solver.py, criterion_preview.py).
   Plus the contention policy 9305 asks for.
2. **Hand-written per-field, per-direction reconciler differs** (~77). Asymmetric ADD-only
   differs, direction inversions, silent pagination truncation, untyped transport (cc77
   names the type gap as the root cause of a357's class). Mitigation: typed transport
   protocol (mypy-enforced port completeness — cc77), roundtrip/property invariants
   (inbound∘outbound identity, direction preservation), pagination-by-construction (one
   paged iterator, no raw page calls).
3. **The gates are themselves a top bug surface** (~100 across plan-review/code-review/
   verifier): attestation staleness/races, verdict non-determinism (620b, e458), token-cap
   INDETERMINATEs, FP classes. Meta-fragility: guardrail bugs erode trust and consume the
   bug budget. Mitigation: treat gate reliability as a product area (it is trending that
   way), keep the FP-ledger/eval loop growing, prefer deterministic pre-checks before LLM
   passes.
4. **Silent-failure default** (~39): fail-open checks, exit-0-on-error, unread env keys,
   integrations broken for weeks unnoticed (1630: 4119 mail errors since 06-30; 8070:
   canary red since 07-14). Mitigation: fail-loud policy for gate/infra code paths +
   auto-file tickets on canary red transitions (pattern already exists for binding-drift/
   heartbeat).

## Q3 — Gate levers, precision-first. Yes: mostly deterministic, narrowly-scoped ones.

Current posture is good: code review blocks only on security + secret/high-critical
detectors; the rest is advisory; plan-review criteria carry applicability gates and ANTI-FP
clauses; an FP ledger polices code-review noise. Levers, ranked by signal-to-noise:
1. **Deterministic CI lint: no raw git writes outside the canonical store seam** (catches
   the 3a33/3435/4dd2 class; low-FP *with* an allowlist for the seam itself and
   test-fixture repos, and scoped to include workflows/scripts — see Q2 §1 for why).
2. **Engine-layer enforcement rule as a code-review project criterion** (narrow): new
   validation/gates must live in the engine, not the CLI layer — catches the 0e15/376d and
   "CLI-only flag" parity class. Deterministic alternative: a parity test template.
3. **"Config key must be observably read" check** — for each new config/env key, require a
   test or a registry entry proving a behavioral effect; the env-registry drift gate
   already exists but checks documentation only (`scripts/gen_env_registry.py`), and b00f
   shows scanner blind spots.
4. **Auto-file P1 tickets on external/live canary red transitions** (8070 sat red for two
   weeks) — observability, but it closes the "merged broken, nobody looked" channel.
   Reuse the reconcile-bridge canary's find-existing-open-ticket→comment dedup pattern
   (reconcile-bridge-canary.yml:259-267) so it cannot spam; external-integration.yml has
   no such path today.
5. **Narrow advisory code-review criterion: absolute wall-clock assertions in tests**
   (edfe/b228/19d7/5e94/85c3 class) — textually detectable, low FP as a scoped rule.
6. **Extend the FP-ledger pattern to plan review** — precision lever for existing criteria
   rather than a new detector; build on the adjudication corpus + FP-proxy harness already
   in docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/.
7. Candidate only — needs a security design first: completion verifier executing a
   ticket's recorded `verify_commands` deterministically before the LLM pass would turn
   "AC satisfied" from pure judgment into judgment + executed evidence and catch
   proxy-validation escapes at close. But verify_commands are agent-authored arbitrary
   shell run in whichever environment closes the ticket: it needs sandboxing/allowlisting
   and a staleness story (plan-time commands vs post-merge tree) before it is a lever, not
   a liability.
Anti-levers: no new blocking LLM dimensions (T9/T5b stay advisory — concurrency/reliability
review by LLM is FP-prone); no mutation-testing gate in CI (keep manual/scoped); no
mandatory local review-code preflight (cost without vote).

## Q4 — rebar-debug: strong on single-bug rigor; four gaps for class-level closure.

The two-phase protocol, falsifiability, dynamic-proof rule, parsimony/exit gate, not-a-bug
guard, and Step 7 sibling sweep are all present and good. Gaps vs "sibling issues,
recurrence through different channels, residual fragility":
1. **No ticket-store writeback.** The skill never claims the bug ticket, records the proven
   root cause + experiment log as a comment, closes with the right `--class`, or files
   sibling/residual tickets with links. Note this is partly deliberate: the skill's
   Approval gate (SKILL.md:94-106) requires user approval before writing to "Jira or other
   trackers". So the fix must reconcile with that gate, not bypass it: add a "Record the
   outcome" section that treats the project's own rebar store as the sanctioned write
   surface when project guidance (AGENTS.md) mandates recording work there, keeping the
   approval gate for external trackers (Jira). Content: root-cause comment (mechanism,
   citations, experiments), close with the taxonomy class, siblings → tickets linked to
   the anchor bug, residual risks → tickets. This is also what makes Q1's recurrence
   observability free.
2. **Step 7 sweeps constructs, not channels.** It greps for the same code construct; the
   observed recurrences are the same *invariant* violated via a different surface (CLI vs
   MCP vs import; local vs CI — a4b2 fixed the local wedge, 449f documents the CI-side
   residue). Add: derive the sweep from the violated invariant, and enumerate parallel
   surfaces (CLI/lib/MCP/workflow/import/CI scripts) and other writers of the same state —
   "who else enforces or relies on this invariant?"
3. **Residual-fragility disposition.** Reporting covers bounded sweeps, but confirmed
   adjacent weaknesses from Phase 1 (dossier leads that weren't the root cause but are real)
   and known-uncovered residue of the fix have no required disposition. Add: a "residual
   risk" line in Reporting + file tickets for confirmed adjacent defects instead of
   dropping them (449f is the exemplar of why).
4. **No class-prevention hook.** When the cause is a repeatable pattern, Step 7 fixes live
   instances but never asks "can this class be made impossible or detectable?" (lint, type,
   constructor, CI gate, FP-ledger entry when a gate mis-fired). Add one paragraph: propose
   the structural guard as a ticket (not inline scope-creep).
Keep additions conditional (writeback only where a rebar store exists — the skill is
cross-project) and short; the skill already warns against ceremony inflation.

## Q5 — rebar-implement: five escape-rate additions that don't duplicate gates.

Held-out TDD, RED-first, mutation/refactoring litmus, preflight, stacked landing are all in
place; plan review owns plan quality, code review owns security/tests/scope advisories, the
verifier owns AC satisfaction, CI owns lint/type/module-size/suite. Escaped classes that
none of those own, addressable in the skill:
1. **Surface-parity enumeration in 4a.** When the behavior exists on multiple surfaces
   (CLI/lib/MCP), the spec must enumerate them and either cover each or explicitly file a
   follow-up ticket (create + link discovered_from). Targets the proven parity class
   (6e88/1598/5199/0e15/376d). No gate checks this today.
2. **"New config is read" oracle rule in 4b.** Any new config key/env var/flag gets one
   test proving behavior differs when it is set (kills 281f/b00f "parsed but read by
   nothing"). The CI env-registry gate checks documentation, not effect.
3. **Contention edge case in tier selection.** If a leaf mutates the ticket store or other
   shared state, the held-out edge set includes one second-writer/contention case —
   authored to test-design §7's deterministic-barrier discipline (multiple real processes,
   barrier/failpoint, no sleeps), else waived. The discipline matters: the repo's newest
   flaky-test close (08-01) is itself a contention test, and an undisciplined mandate here
   would feed the ~41-bug CI-flakiness cluster. Scoped to the store's dominant bug class,
   not a general mandate.
4. **Gate-finding → oracle upgrade loop in 4g.** On any post-push Verified -1 or LLM
   finding that is real, record in the session log which held-out test should have caught
   it and add that case before amending — converts every escape into a permanent oracle
   member.
5. **Residual-gap disposition at close.** If an edge/E2E case was deliberately descoped,
   file the ticket before closing the leaf (extends the existing discovered_from rule from
   "missing dependency" to "known untested residue").
Anti-additions: no mandatory local `review-code` preflight, no mutation-testing runs per
leaf, no re-statement of module-size/lint (already in the 4d brief and CI).

Completed this session: finished the change-by-change operator review (all 25 proposals decided: 20 approved, 3 rejected, 1 withdrawn, 1 merged); created all 17 epic children with full plan-template descriptions; recorded links (b967 depends_on d3ed; e602 relates_to d37e; e931 relates_to cc77; ad0d relates_to 78f1); set file_impact on epic + all children; closed idea e71b-1a38-bf7a-4de0 as superseded; wrote the full decision table to session log 5eb0-52a3-45f0-43e5.

Child index: d3ed detected-by | b967 bug_trends lens | 433c AC-precheck | d37e raw-git lint | a584 engine-layer criterion | 6754 config-is-read DET | 1e95 wall-clock detector | e931 reconciler property tests | e602/f1eb/9d07 shell-to-Python Tiers 3/2/1 | 4527 canary hardening | ad0d bug-fix plan review (B1 exemption narrowing + B2 Gerrit DET backstop) | 78f1 rebar-debug prose | 7359 rebar-implement + test-design prose | fa6e read-under-storm property | b047 comment hygiene + CI guard.

comments.body: Change 26 (post-epic addition, operator-proposed): epic-close bug gate -> ticket 4b54-6e28-45f7-42db under epic 2f4c. Evaluated the proposal logically and against the event-level record (STATUS events from the tickets branch, not updated_at proxies — two adjudications corrected: 22f5 was fixed in-epic before close; 5e94 was created 13 days post-close). Real at-close escapes: 30a2, 5b09 (2/56 closes). Design: DET caused_by floor + DET candidate filter (created-after-first-in_progress OR linked-any-depth; commit-relation criterion rejected on evidence: 0 unique catches, 2 FPs, 58% cited-SHA rot) + single-turn haiku forced-choice screen (cached epic prefix, warm-then-parallel, model-class config) forwarding max 8 compact candidates to the completion verifier, which adjudicates via its native show_ticket tool and blocks only undispositioned deliverable-defects. Screen tally recorded in sidecar; degrades open; regression set encoded in the ticket. Backtest scripts: /tmp/bt_epic_bugs.py, /tmp/bt_filter.py, /tmp/bt_c3b.py.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Rich-text (Markdown⇄Jira) conversion — brainstorm research record (pre-ticket).
Design source-of-truth artifact: session workspace files/rich-text-design-notes.md + 6 spike
scripts/reports. This log captures the durable findings so the plan lives in the store.

GOAL: convert Markdown in rebar descriptions/comments into each Jira client's rich format
(Cloud=ADF, DC=wiki) bidirectionally, WITHOUT a sync echo loop, preferring a library over a
hand-rolled engine.

== CLOUD (ADF) — settled ==
- marklas (pure-Python MD↔ADF, mistune-based, MIT) measured 99.64% fixed-point over 5,568 real
  historical bodies (vs DIY mistune 90.7%). ADOPT.
- 0.36% failures = 2 true strong+strikethrough mark-order oscillators; ~18 transient. AC: fix the
  2 oscillators (canonicalize ADF mark arrays), accept the ~18 transient as settled.
- Supply-chain risk: marklas is single-author, ~5 months old, near-zero adoption, only pure-Python
  bidirectional MD↔ADF lib (research spike). AC: VENDOR/FORK + pin by hash; abandonment contingency.
- ADF+marklas IS the robust "structured target + typed-node passthrough" pattern → stays truly
  lossless bidirectional.

== DC (wiki) — PIVOTED after spikes + repo-cost constraint ==
Original direction (self-verifying / segmenting partial codec) is SUPERSEDED. Why:
- pandoc via pypandoc MD↔wiki is lossy: raw whole-body fixed-point only 72% (94.86% w/ escape-
  collapse), residual = pandoc MISPARSING literal punctuation-dense prose. ADF is lossless JSON;
  wiki is lossy text — asymmetry is FUNDAMENTAL, no library fixes it.
- Self-verify codec (render rich iff the unit's own round-trip is a proven fixed point, else plain)
  = 100% echo-safe but only ~15% whole-body coverage.
- Segmenting partial codec (per-block/item self-verify + passthrough) reaches ~72% of bodies BUT
  the true WIRE round-trip (decode from the stored string only) proved it FRAGILE:
  * native {noformat}/{code} envelopes INFEASIBLE — pandoc emits those markers for real code, so a
    converted code block is byte-indistinguishable from a passthrough wrapper (structural collision
    on 1.2% of bodies). Only a non-pandoc SENTINEL survives — not human-editable, breaks on global
    re-pandoc, truncatable by a stray marker.
  * NOT a clean fixed point: 76.5% strict; 23.5% drift@1 then stable (whitespace + pandoc <!-- -->,
    0 content loss). Eventually-idempotent, not fixed-point.
  * Slow ratchet: pandoc accretes one backslash per round-trip inside inline code; a single-pass
    normalize check certifies it while it diverges forever → self-verify would need raw rt2==rt1.
- OSS RELIABILITY RESEARCH: NO production project does a reliable flat-string sentinel segmenting
  codec over a lossy text format bidirectionally. Robust systems use (1) structured target + typed
  passthrough (Confluence storage XHTML <ac:structured-macro>, confmark <!--cf-raw:-->, Sanity
  Portable Text _type, mdast html) or (3) source-of-truth + STATE-based echo suppression (jirafs git
  shadow-blob diff; git-bug actor-id + LastSync; Exalate/Unito revision watermark). pandoc has NO
  Jira reader by design. Flat-string sentinel over DC wiki CANNOT be made non-fragile.

PIVOT (conditionally accepted, pending experiments): DC codec = ONE-WAY MD→wiki render (pandoc +
two safe lossless wins) + rebar's EXISTING STATE-based echo suppression. rebar is already Pattern 3:
ADR 0026 per-binding baseline stores the last-synced Jira-side value incl. description
(binding_store.py:_BASELINE_FIELDS), changing 0 entries/pass when stable (epic 0303). So echo is
suppressed by comparing Jira's current value to stored baseline — NOT by decode(encode(x))==x. The
sentinel/23.5% drift/backslash ratchet stop being echo-safety problems (display-quality only;
normalize-before-compare à la Jupyter nbformat.normalize). DC gives up LOSSLESS INBOUND rich decode
(structurally infeasible) but keeps bidirectional SYNC. Conflict policy = LAST-WRITE-WINS, with
tests ensuring neither side's changes are erroneously destroyed.

Two safe lossless wins (adopt on the outbound render):
- Code-aware ARROW substitution (-> <- <-> => to → ← ↔ ⇒, prose-only, skips fenced/inline code):
  arrows are in 30.7% of bodies and churn to -\> ; Unicode round-trips perfectly; +2.3pp WB,
  0 masking. (Danger-census: arrows gate 21.6% of corpus as their ONLY danger class.)
- Verbatim-WRAP ASCII tables in {noformat}: baseline ASCII tables ERODE one dash per round-trip
  (66/70 data loss); wrap is echo-safe 70/70 and stops the erosion class. (User accepts tables
  not converting.)
DROP inline-span granularity (+0.1pp for 85/300 seam corruptions). Ship DESCRIPTIONS before
comments (descriptions convert 30% chars/100% some-rich vs comments 23.6%/63.3%).

== HARD CONSTRAINT: repo performance (in-flight epic 0303) ==
tickets branch = 1.04 GiB; 92% is the committed .bridge_state cache (events 55 MB). Must stay
committed (ephemeral runners); content & churn are the levers, not location. Bloat came from a
per-pass TIMESTAMP (baseline_advanced_at, 1144 entries/pass) scattered across a sort-ordered 18 MB
bindings.json defeating git delta compression — NOT baseline values (0/pass). DISCIPLINE for our
state: change 0 entries/pass when nothing changed; reuse existing baseline; if a rich-echo signal
is needed add only a FIXED-SIZE, CHANGE-GATED hash of the last-emitted wire (never the full wire,
never a per-pass timestamp); don't fatten baseline[description] (story A3 normalizes it to cut
churn); co-design with 0303's format ADR (A5) + store-epoch guard. NOTE: the OSS research's naive
"store per-issue last_sync_ts each sync" is exactly the 0303 anti-pattern — rejected.

== DEPENDENCIES ==
The DC rich-text epic (to be authored) will DEPEND ON completion of 3 in-flight epics: 0303
(.bridge_state state/format + reclaim), e369 (Jira-family DC seam), 3e73 (Cloud↔DC test parity).

== RUBBER-DUCK BLOCKERS folded into ACs ==
comment identity by body-set is broken (needs persistent Jira-comment-ID map); origin-gating
doesn't protect native ADF after a local edit (structural merge / block-when-native-nodes);
normalization must stay COMPARE-ONLY (never a local write → git churn / gate retrigger); keep
jira_emit separate from compare values; keep normalize_rich_text back-compat for sibling repo
agentic-dev-platform (it imports it); live-oracle gap — offline pandoc/marklas ≠ Jira's own
canonicalization, must test real POST→GET and rendered HTML not just REST source.

== EXPERIMENTS IN FLIGHT (parallel subagents) to prove the pivot ==
1. Echo-suppression + LWW-safety simulation (0 self-echo; rebar-only/Jira-only/concurrent edits;
   neither side erroneously destroyed).
2. Git-delta storage-cost (0303 methodology: replay revisions + repack + marginal KB/version;
   gate = baseline-value churn profile, not timestamp).
3. Cross-project generalization + final codec numbers (frozen renderer over our + sibling corpora).
4. Live-oracle DC harness extension (extend tests/external/live_jira_dc/, assert rendered HTML).

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Rich-text DC PIVOT — all 4 de-risking experiments PASSED (parallel subagents; scripts+reports in session files/).
1) Echo-suppression+LWW: n=800; self-echo 0 spurious re-syncs / 0 local rewrites; concurrent edits 799/799 conflicts DETECTED, 0 silently destroyed; norm() masks 0 real changes. CRITICAL AC: baseline = value OBSERVED AFTER push (Jira's canonical form), not raw wire sent → +1 GET per changed field. One-way design means never inb() in echo path (adversarial out∘inb 32.7% drift is upper bound only).
2) Repo-cost (epic-0303 methodology): change-gated rich_sha=sha256(wire)[:16] (8 bytes) INLINE in bindings.json = 0.07 KB/ver stable, identical to baseline; per-pass timestamp anti-pattern reproduced 0303's 12.79→12.62 KB. Respects churn discipline; full-wire storage rejected.
3) Cross-project generalization: safety perfect+invariant across 23 env_ids/6 authors + OOD cli/cli(489); 0 corruptions; coverage 68.2% bodies/78.5% chars, authors CV<6.4%, OOD over-performs → not overfit. Future guard candidate: OOD HTML density ~30×.
4) Live-oracle: draft test extends existing Docker DC harness (renderedFields HTML fidelity, not just REST source); offline checks pass; live gap (Jira canonicalization/renderer) scoped to jira-dc-harness CI job. IMPL AC: arrow substitution runs on MD BEFORE pandoc.
VERDICT: pivot fully validated. Next: author epic (depends on 0303/e369/3e73). Open decision: comment edit/delete semantics (append-only vs full sync via persistent Jira-comment-ID map).

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:

EPIC 708d-0767-1a51-4928 'Bidirectional Markdown <-> Jira rich-text sync (Cloud ADF + DC wiki)' — depends_on 0303, e369, 3e73 (the 3 in-flight epics). Children:
- e59d Cloud ADF codec (marklas vendored/pinned; strong+strike mark-order fix; ~18 transient accepted)
- 271c DC one-way segmenting wiki renderer (pandoc; arrows-on-MD-before-pandoc; ASCII table {noformat}-wrap; dangerous units passthrough; ~68% bodies/78% chars)
- 5c0e DC robustness/perf (per-call pandoc timeout+verbatim fallback; no-spawn on no-change; GPL/SBOM pin)  [depends_on 271c]
- 3388 State echo suppression + LWW (ADR-0026 observed-after-push baseline; inline 8-byte change-gated rich_sha; 799/799 no-silent-destruction)  [depends_on e59d,271c]
- 789c Comment sync append-only (persistent Jira-comment-ID map; descriptions ship first)  [depends_on 3388]
- 3289 Live DC harness renderedFields HTML + cross-repo normalize_rich_text contract  [depends_on 5c0e,3388]
All 7 pass clarity-check + check-ac. File-impact set on all.
BLOCKER (pre-existing, NOT from this authoring): plan-review LLM gate cannot snapshot — reducer-error on a DANGLING plan-relation 'reference: 211c-45bf-3966-4b61' (a ticket with NO CREATE/SNAPSHOT event; git grep '211c-45bf' on tickets branch = 0 committed matches). Reproduces IDENTICALLY on full review-plan --force for 0303, e369, AND 3e73 — so it is store-wide and independent of the new tickets, not caused by them. Remediation (tool's own): repair/remove the unreadable plan relationship, then rerun review-plan. Not self-fixed: reconciler is live + another session owns those epics; mutating shared relations unilaterally risks collision. review-plan is also legitimately deferred: the epic is not-yet-claimable until 0303/e369/3e73 close, and reviews must run in dependency order once they do.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: RESOLVED the plan-review snapshot blocker. Root cause: two EMPTY, untracked directories in .tickets-tracker/ (211c-45bf-3966-4b61, acd3-837b-6e13-40ed) — debris of an interrupted rebar write (~10:05 today), never committed (hence git grep=0). The LOCAL rebar build (HEAD b301e7, 10 commits behind origin/main) has an OLD relation-snapshot reducer that HARD-FAILS (reducer-error) on an event-less ticket dir, blocking review-plan for every ticket whose dependency-closure walk hit it. origin/main (5892134) FIXED this: it skips such a dir with a WARNING ('debris of an interrupted write; safe to delete') instead of erroring — verified by building origin/main in a throwaway worktree and re-running review-plan (reducer passed; only remaining INDETERMINATE cause = missing [agents] LLM extra). Applied the data-side fix too: rmdir'd both empty debris dirs; the OLD local build now also passes the reducer (indet []). Net: the blocker was environmental (stale local debris + a since-fixed reducer), NOT a defect in the authored DC rich-text tickets. comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
RAN the plan-review LLM gate for real (Bedrock) on the Cloud story e59d — verdict BLOCK, 15 blocking + 10 advisory. llm_ran=True, model bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6, verified against origin/main.
DOMINANT FINDING (E4/G1G2/G6/T1/T3, ~11/15): origin/main ALREADY ships a wired+tested Cloud rich-text stack, landed by dep-epic e369 (story J3) — our tickets were authored against a 10-commit-stale checkout + old design notes and are mis-grounded:
- adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py = RichTextCodec Protocol seam (ADR 0055).
- adapters/jira/rich_text_codec.py = AdfCodec (Cloud's RichTextCodec impl, story J3/e369): to_wire + decode_inbound.
- adapters/jira/adf.py = text_to_adf (275-307) / adf_to_text (26-34).
- adapters/jira_family/outbound_mapper.py takes a RichTextCodec ('AdfCodec for Cloud, <DC> for DC') <- the DC slot is exactly where our DC codec plugs in.
- inbound_fields.normalize_rich_text (134-145) already decodes ADF->PLAIN TEXT; SHARED surface (ticket 21ca).
=> RE-GROUND THE EPIC against origin/main: Cloud premise 'reconciler pushes plain Markdown' is FALSE (it emits ADF); real Cloud gap = make the EXISTING plain-text->ADF encode MARKDOWN-AWARE behind the AdfCodec/RichTextCodec seam (extend adf.py or slot marklas behind AdfCodec), NOT greenfield. DC story = implement a RichTextCodec for DC and plug into outbound_mapper's DC slot, not wire into backend.normalize_rich_text. Also fix E2 (vendor-vs-extra either/or -> default to vendored marklas w/ recorded sha), drop refuted premises, add Prior-art subsections, verify marklas claims by reading tree.
Other findings: E5/E6 cutover of live outbound path needs a failure-path + live end-to-end test; T5b external-integration failure point; symbol-reference-completeness on normalize_rich_text.
NOTE on WHY it hadn't run before: not a policy hold. The rebar on PATH is a STALE pipx install (pre-Bedrock, resolves anthropic:claude-* direct w/ no key, and its anthropic SDK is version-incompatible with pydantic_ai 1.38 -> ImportError UserLocation). Ran it via a fresh origin/main worktree venv (/tmp/rebar-omain) with pip install -e '.[agents]' + 'pydantic-ai-slim[bedrock]' + boto3, env REBAR_LLM_{FRONTIER,STANDARD,TRIVIAL}_MODEL=bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-{opus-4-8,sonnet-4-6,haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0} + REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION=us-east-1 (AWS creds live; converse OK 1.3s). Store-wide overlap pre-pass is CPU-heavy (~4-5 min) before any LLM call on this ~3000-ticket store.
